documents.title: Respiration in Living Organisms
documents.subject: Biology
facts: Respiration is a chemical process that releases energy from glucose inside living cells.
Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water while releasing energy.
The word equation is: glucose plus oxygen produces carbon dioxide plus water and energy.
Breathing and respiration are different. Breathing moves air into and out of the lungs, while respiration occurs inside cells.
Living organisms need released energy for movement, growth, repair, active transport and maintaining body temperature.
misconceptions: The lungs do not create energy from oxygen.
Carbon dioxide is produced during aerobic respiration; it is not used as the main reactant.
